title: The Trip Point — Editor Intro
summary: Opening splash shifts the danger from remote authority to local responsibility: distributed control only works if limits still hold when people have reasons to push past them.
panelPlan: Full-page opening/title splash centered on ordinary community water controls in hard daylight: mechanical gauges, a physical limit mark, access hardware and visible piping, all functional and maintained.
Frame local hands and tools near the system without showing misuse. The tension should come from the proximity of authority to consequence.
Echo the rocket world only as a distant silhouette or small work artifact so the page joins engineering and governance without previewing the vehicle-control plot.
Give TRUST IS NOT A CONTROL SYSTEM its own strong typographic field immediately before the title.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Public Sky was built to remove a dangerous kind of permission: the kind that lives far away from the people who pay the price.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: A limit only matters if it survives the moment somebody desperately wants around it.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: A safeguard only matters if the people who built it are willing to be stopped by it.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Trust is not a control system.

directionInline.text: Non-diegetic opening title page. Preserve exact caption text. Do not depict a damaged pump, a defeated limit, the maintenance shortcut, a public confession, a two-party rule, a flight result or any other Issue 4 reveal. The page should make responsibility feel dangerous before the story shows why.
